headline: Silver Mines' Bowdens project on track for development consent by end of 2025, with 2027 shaping as a seminal year for financing and construction decisions.
reasoning: The Bowdens silver project in New South Wales lost its development consent in a 2023 Court of Appeal decision on a technical matter. Silver Mines has since responded to government RFIs and submitted all required information at the end of June, with the decision now in the government's hands. If consent is granted by end of calendar year 2025, the company expects 2027 to be pivotal for front-end engineering design, financing, and a financial investment decision. The feasibility study outlines a mine life of more than 25 years, pre-production capital of $455 million, and was engineered conservatively with a $35/oz silver price assumption versus a spot price of approximately $59/oz at the time of the interview. Financing is expected to follow a conventional 50/50 or 60/40 debt-to-equity split, and the strong current silver price environment is seen as a tailwind for securing debt funding.
quote: The key is the development consent. I mean, if we can have that by, you know, end of the year, end of this calendar year. That puts us in a very good position to, for 2027 to be a very sort of seminal year for silver mines with respect to front end engineering, design, financing, you know, financial investment decision and, and funding. We believe that this project is sufficiently robust from an economic perspective that, you know, the risks are really contained around the silver price. And to mitigate against those risks, you know, the study that we released yesterday, we believe has been done to a very conservative nature with a silver price assumption in the mine design of $35 US dollars. I think this morning it's 59.
episode_title: Silver lining for Silver Mines as Bowdens edges closer to development

headline: Silver Mines offers significant catch-up trade as Bowdens consent recovery, DFS upgrade and rising silver price create re-rating catalyst
reasoning: Silver Mines lost its development consent in August 2024, which caused the share price to fall 50%. Since then, silver prices have more than doubled, the company has released a DFS with a larger reserve, longer mine life, and improved economics, and the consent has been recovered. Battershill argues the stock has not yet caught up with these developments and trades at a significant discount to global silver peers that was justified by the consent loss but is no longer warranted. Engineering studies used a conservative $35/oz silver price, well below the spot price of ~$58-60 and consensus of $45-47, providing downside protection. At $40-45/oz silver, the project generates very strong returns once in production, and lifting the design price to $50/oz increases contained silver by 35%, highlighting strong leverage to rising prices.
quote: When we lost our development consent back in August 2024, our share price fell 50%. Subsequent to that, silver price has more than doubled. We've now released a DFS, which demonstrates a much, much more significant reserve position in my life and production profile with starkly different and improved economic fundamentals. So getting the consent back is obviously a key driving factor of this stock. We fell 50% given those subsequent developments in the silver market and the balanced development profile. Since we lost the consent, I think there's a significant catch up trade. And when I look at our global peers and unfortunately there's not really many peers in Australia, silver is a bit of an orphan commodity in Australia. But when you look at our global peers, we traded a significant discount to those peers on the basis of having lost the consent.
episode_title: Silver lining for Silver Mines as Bowdens edges closer to development

headline: Silver price at ~$59/oz provides strong tailwind for silver project financing and development economics, well above conservative $35/oz mine design assumption.
reasoning: The spot silver price at the time of the interview was approximately $59/oz and pushing back towards $60, compared to the conservative $35/oz price used in the Bowdens mine design. The elevated silver price environment is seen as highly supportive for securing debt financing and improving project economics, with sensitivities showing materially stronger returns if the mine design price assumption is lifted to $50/oz or above. The speaker noted that funding the project over the prior 12 months would not have been problematic given the silver price strength.
quote: We're very conscious that, you know, the pre-production capital of $455 million is going to require a certain element of debt and equity and whatever that split is, is yet to be decided. The debt funding, you know, debt funders require a slightly more conservative approach to pricing assumptions in development studies. So, you know, we very much engineered this study to be acceptable for from a risk management perspective for potential debt providers. Having a having a high silver price with a, with a bit of a tailwind is always very useful. You know, if we'd been trying to fund this project in the last 12 months, it wouldn't be a problem at all.
episode_title: Silver lining for Silver Mines as Bowdens edges closer to development

headline: Silver price strength well above engineering design assumptions provides strong buffer for development-stage silver projects
reasoning: Battershill notes spot silver is around $58-60/oz while consensus pricing sits at $45-47/oz and the trailing two-year price is also ~$47/oz. The Bowdens DFS was engineered at a conservative $35/oz silver price, meaning the project has significant headroom before economics are impaired. He highlights that silver is an 'orphan commodity' in Australia with few local peers, suggesting limited domestic investment options for silver exposure despite strong price performance.
quote: Spot price is 60, or 58. Consensus pricing is 45 to 47. The trailing two year price is 47 as well. So we're well below those levels from a from an engineering design, which should give comfort to potential investors that if the silver price was to weaken whilst we were in the construction phase, it's not that much of an issue. And at a 40 to $45 silver price, once we're in production, the project generates very, very strong returns. So it is a very leveraged play.
episode_title: Silver lining for Silver Mines as Bowdens edges closer to development
